dossiers.thesis_summary: Wave Life Sciences holds an FDA-GRANTED, not-yet-held meeting to discuss a potential accelerated-approval pathway for WVE-006 (GalNAc RNA editing) in alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency. Verified verbatim in the 30 July 2026 Q2 release: the meeting request "was granted by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA)" and "is scheduled for the end of summer 2026." The event is real, idiosyncratic (resolves on Wave's own AAT biomarker package and FDA judgement, not the tape), and UNFIRED as of 4 August 2026 - but it has slipped a full quarter (Wave's 18 May 2026 release guided "regulatory feedback ... mid-2026"), it is season-dated rather than calendar-dated, it is non-binding (minutes and guidance, no decision, no payout), and minutes customarily arrive ~30 days post-meeting, pointing disclosure into the company's own "investor day in the fall of 2026." The load-bearing asymmetry is not probability but PAYOFF: Beam Therapeutics already secured FDA alignment on a biomarker-based accelerated pathway for BEAM-302 in the same indication on 25 March 2026 (12-month AAT biomarker endpoint, 60 mg dose), so a favourable Wave answer is confirmation of an established agency precedent, not a revelation. Re-derived on live numbers the name prices roughly at fair value: 0.45 x $7.75 + 0.55 x $4.10 = $5.74 versus a $5.74 last, i.e. essentially zero expected edge, against the board's +20.6%.
dossiers.kill_risk: The most load-bearing claim in the thesis is that a favourable FDA answer pays. It may not. Three live facts push against it. (1) PRECEDENT ALREADY SET: Beam obtained FDA alignment on an AAT-biomarker accelerated pathway for BEAM-302 on 25 March 2026, so "FDA open to biomarker AA in AATD" is priced knowledge; Wave winning re-rates the company only to the extent its own levels look competitive. (2) THEY DO NOT: on Wave's own 18 May 2026 numbers, functional wild-type M-AAT is 11.9 uM x 64.4% = 7.7 uM (200 mg biweekly) and 13.6 uM x 58.7% = 8.0 uM (400 mg monthly) - both BELOW the ~11 uM augmentation-therapy protective threshold, versus Beam's 16.1 uM total at 94% M-AAT = ~15.1 uM functional. The agency can grant the endpoint class and still require a dose/level Wave has not yet shown, which converts a "win" into a reset timeline pending the 600 mg monthly cohort. (3) NO CLEAN DISCLOSURE EVENT: minutes are private, ~30 days post-meeting, and the company's stated venue is a fall investor day - Wave controls both the timing and the framing, so the "resolution" can arrive as a bundled narrative slide rather than a printable answer. Residual: the position can be right on the science and still collect no repricing.

dossiers.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim is "an unfired, mechanically-due pivotal binary with defined downside". Both halves are attackable from the live record. (1) The price has already discounted the win: on my legs the breakeven probability is (20.17-2.50)/(30-2.50) = 64.3%, above my 62% fundamental estimate, so the expected value is roughly flat-to-slightly-negative rather than the +45% the board carries - the edge was in the $8-14 tape, not at a 52-week high. (2) The evidentiary prior is thinner than "pivotal-ready" implies: the supporting work is a Phase 2 PREVENT crossover of N=18 (40-55% event reduction) and an N=16 open-label investigator-initiated Phase 2b; a 78-patient parallel-group read on a variable, event-count endpoint with real placebo response is not the same experiment, and Breakthrough designation is not evidence of effect size. (3) The downside is not defined in any protective sense: the same management team's prior binary (AMX0035 PHOENIX) closed $18.97 on 7 Mar 2024 and $3.36 on 8 Mar 2024, -82% in one session, resting at $1.62 by June 2024 - and that shell held more cash per share than AMLX will hold at the LUCIDITY print, so $2.50 is a mark, not a floor; $1.60-2.00 is inside precedent.
